From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@hydraai.com>

Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent — upcoming model release + request for extra tranche capacity

Mina,

Quick note: we're going to cut the 2.1 release next week and traffic forecasts show a 3x increase for inference during peak hours for at least the first 3 weeks. We talked previously about the dedicated tranche (8xA100) from HYD-2028-37, but that won't cover the burst. Can Redwood short-term provision an additional 4x A100 for dedicated use (or allow preemptible burst on the same pool) for the 14–21 May window?

We understand there are contention policies — this is time-boxed and tied to our launch. If necessary we can accept a temporary SLA exception and a pricing uplift. Please advise on feasibility and next steps — we need confirmation to finalize our rollout plan by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Engineering, HydraAI

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700

Team — forwarding Hydra's ask. Key facts: deal HYD-2028-37 is a Q2 Dedicated contract with a committed 8x A100 tranche and reserved burst rules stated in the SOW. They want +4xA100 for 14–21 May or burst on the same pool. They explicitly said they'd accept a temporary SLA exception and pricing uplift.

Questions I have before I respond to Alex:
- Do we have spare unallocated 4x A100 in us-west region in that window, even if preemptible?
- If not, what are the options: shift capacity from lower-priority deals, enable cross-region routing (latency risk), or provide a short-term burst with uplift and throttled fairness?
- If we grant, do we require a formal temporary SLA exception doc?

Rishi / Vivek — can you please run a fast availability check (preferred by EOD) and propose 2 options (conservative & aggressive) I can present to the customer?

Mina
Director, Account Success — Dedicated Customers
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

On Thu, May 9, 2028 at 10:03 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Hydra's ask. Key facts: deal HYD-2028-37 is a Q2 Dedicated contract with a committed 8x A100 tranche and reserved burst rules stated in the SOW. They want +4xA100 for 14–21 May or burst on the same pool. They explicitly said they'd accept a temporary SLA exception and pricing uplift.
>
> Questions I have before I respond to Alex:
> - Do we have spare unallocated 4x A100 in us-west region in that window, even if preemptible?
>
I ran a quick check against the capacity calendar and our allocation ledger. Short answer: not enough non-reserved stock in us-west to guarantee 4x A100 contiguous for the entire window. We can offer either:

Option A (conservative): 4x A100 preemptible burst routed to their Dedicated pool with best-effort preemption protection. Will require a temporary SLA exception and explicit throttling above committed QPS. No other customers will be preempted, this is best-effort and we can only promise >=60% availability across the window.

Option B (aggressive): Temporarily reassign 4x A100 from a lower-priority reserved tranche (deal: PEREGRINE-2028-09, medium priority) for the 7-day window. This requires approvals from Capacity Ops lead and a preemption notice to the other customer. Availability would be ~95% and lower latency. There's an operational cost for migration and potential credits to the affected customer.

I recommend we offer Option A immediately and concurrently fast-track Option B if Hydra confirms willingness to sign an SLA exception plus uplift and accept a small credit contingency for the other party.

Rishi
Capacity Planning Manager
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@hydraai.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 14:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — upcoming model release + request for extra tranche capacity

Mina — thanks. We prefer Option B (full performance) and will accept an uplift and a documented SLA exception to guarantee the tranche for 14–21 May. We can't risk degraded latency for our customers during launch. Please advise next steps and what approvals you need. We can sign an addendum today if that speeds things up.

Alex
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HydraAI urgent capacity prioritization & tranche sizing request

Mina / Rishi — I'm escalating this to Capacity Ops leadership and Legal for a controlled preemption. Quick summary of my recommendation:

1) Approve Option B for 14–21 May conditioned on:
   - Hydra signs a one-week addendum (SLA exception + 30% uplift for that window).
   - We issue a 48-hour notice to the lower-priority tranche owner (PEREGRINE-2028-09) with migration/runbook support.
   - We commit to a credit cap if the migration causes sustained unavailability beyond 6 hours.

2) Run a mitigation checklist: cross-zone placement to avoid single rack failure, KV cache warmup run 24 hours prior, and adjust autoscaling thresholds so Hydra's pool can't monopolize shared batchers.

3) Contingency: If PEREGRINE refuses migration, fallback to Option A and inform Hydra within 6 hours.

I will notify Legal and Ops now. Marcus, Soojin — can you prepare the draft addendum and the customer notification template? I want this reflected in HubSpot and the capacity calendar by EOD.

Vivek
VP, Dedicated Products
